note: Engraved elevation plates from 19th-century French architectural publications OTHER than Daly. What unites them is that they are measurable: each carries a scale bar, printed dimensions, or a sectional storey ladder. Daly is one publication in one year (1864); these are independent draughtsmen, publishers and dates, which is the only way to tell a Daly convention apart from a Paris fact. Extended by a bounded crawl of archimaps.tumblr.com/search/paris (15 pages, 223 posts). YIELD FOR THE SECOND EMPIRE WAS THIN: that blog's Paris tag runs heavily to monuments, theatres, churches, expositions and interiors, and the immeuble elevations it does carry are mostly 1890s-1900s. The one Second Empire commercial sheet it holds is bd de Sebastopol 72 -- which the operator had already supplied by hand.
provenance_warning: All three were supplied by the operator from image reposts (Tumblr, a print reseller). The ENGRAVINGS are long out of copyright; the scans' hosts and rights are not recorded. Treat the drawing as evidence and the attribution as a lead until an original scan is located.

images.title: Maison, boulevard de Sébastopol n° 72 — élévation
images.author: Th. Vacquer del.; Lemaître fils sculp.; Brodard imp.; Paris, Caudrilier éditeur, Rue St Martin 19
images.year: unrecorded on the sheet — the Moniteur's 60e volume dates it, and that volume year is not yet established
images.shows: A commercial frontage on the SAME BOULEVARD as six of the Daly anchors (1, 2 et 4, 63, 77, 87, 120), drawn by a different hand for a different publication. Shop ground floor, entresol with cartouches (A·M and 72), four etages, mansard with segmental lucarnes, a balcon filant at the 2e and another at the 5e.
images.why_it_matters: PRINTED DIMENSIONS, not scale-bar readings. 17.55 m is exactly the 1859 reglement's cornice for the 12-20 m street band and exactly what Daly measures at 1 bd de Sebastopol -- an independent publication landing on the same number is the strongest corroboration in the register. It also carries a 10-metre scale bar, so the printed figures can be checked against the drawing.

images.title: Maison à Paris, rue de Rennes — façade principale
images.author: Maurage sc.; Imp. Lemercier et Cie
images.architect: BOUSSARD (partial reading — the credit line is clipped by the scan's bottom edge)
images.year: 1881 (printed on the sheet; a publication date, i.e. a DESIGN date, not a construction date)
images.shows: A dated PRE-1884 commercial frontage, twenty-two years after the 1859 reglement and three years before Alphand -- the long middle of the chronology, which had no plate at all between Daly's 1864 and the 1887 anchor.
images.why_it_matters: Carries a scale bar (0-9 m). The 1887 anchor is a 340px thumbnail: datable but not measurable. This is the only dated AND measurable sheet outside 1864 in the register.
images.open_question: Bears on the unresolved upper-floor sill (A21): a scale bar separates allege, light and lintel bearing directly, where the Daly reconstruction can only subtract them and comes out noisy (0.21-1.76 m across 32 readings).

images.title: Maison de rapport, petits appartements — avenue Duquesne, à Paris
images.publication: A. Lévy, éditeur, r. de Seine 29 — V.2, PL. 36
images.author: E. Japhet del.; Maurage fils sc.; Imp. Lemercier et Cie
images.shows: A maison de rapport of PETITS APPARTEMENTS -- a cheaper programme than anything in Daly's selection, which is drawn from a luxury journal and biased toward exemplars.
images.why_it_matters: Two things nothing else in the register has. A PRINTED TOTAL COST, which is the only direct evidence of what a programme actually cost and therefore of what 'class' means in money rather than in ornament. And a VERTICAL SECTION STRIP down the right-hand margin showing every floor slab -- a storey ladder of the kind Daly prints only twice.
images.limits: No scale bar located on the sheet; the section strip gives storey RATIOS, and an absolute needs one dimension from elsewhere.

images.shows: Shop ground floor under five residential storeys, continuous balconies, mansard. A clean full elevation.

images.title: Entrance door and bow window — large-scale detail
images.period: LATE — the draughtsmanship and ornament read 1890s-1900s (Art Nouveau / Belle Epoque), NOT Second Empire. Filed for the post-1902 end of the chronology; it is not evidence for the 1859-1884 core.

images.title: Maison Montmorency — elevation, section and plans
images.architect: NOT ESTABLISHED from the sheet at the resolution available.
images.period: EARLY — classical, reads pre-Haussmann. A candidate anchor for the far side of the 1859 règlement, which the register has nothing for.
images.shows: Elevation, section AND plans on one sheet, with a scale.

images.title: Maison, boulevard Haussmann — façade
images.period: SECOND EMPIRE — two years after Daly's 1864 corpus, under the same 1859 reglement.
images.publication: A. Lévy, r. de Seine 29; Ch. Chardon aîné imp.; A. Normand direx.
images.shows: Full coloured façade: rusticated base with a carriage arch, four storeys, mansard with segmental lucarnes, individual garde-corps at every window and a balcon filant.
images.why_it_matters: The closest sheet in date to the Daly corpus from a DIFFERENT publisher. Coloured, so it also carries joinery and ironwork tone, which Daly's engravings do not.

images.title: Maison, avenue de l'Opéra — façade
images.period: THIRD REPUBLIC, pre-Alphand — inside the 1859 regime.
images.publication: Imp. Lemercier et Cie; Martel sc.
images.shows: Avenue frontage: continuous glazed commercial ground floor, five storeys, oeil-de-boeuf lucarnes in the mansard, balcons filants.
images.why_it_matters: Carries a printed SCALE BAR, so it is measurable. Fills 1879, between the 1866 sheet and 1885.

images.title: Maison à Paris, boulevard Saint-Germain 21 — élévation sur rue
images.period: THIRD REPUBLIC, ONE YEAR AFTER the Alphand decree of 23 July 1884.
images.shows: A rich boulevard frontage with a deep glazed ground floor, caryatid-flanked entrance and a heavily modelled upper facade.
images.why_it_matters: Carries a printed SCALE BAR, so it is measurable. TWO THINGS. It is on boulevard Saint-Germain, where Daly measures no. 6 — same street, twenty-one years apart. And it is by the SAME ARCHITECT as the 1881 rue de Rennes sheet in this family: Boussard at 1881 and again at 1885, on either side of the Alphand decree. That is a natural control for the H83/H87 discontinuity — one hand, one city, one rule changed between them.

images.title: Maison, avenue Friedland à Paris — façade
images.publication: Moniteur des Architectes; Alice Sulpis sc.
images.shows: Coloured façade, a grand avenue building with a heavily sculpted centre bay and a carriage entrance.
images.why_it_matters: Coloured, and by a woman engraver (Alice Sulpis) — worth noting because the register's attributions are otherwise uniformly male.

images.title: Maison, avenue des Champs-Élysées
images.period: NOT ESTABLISHED — the drawing convention reads Second Empire but that is a judgement, not a date.
images.publication: dessiné et publié par V. Calliat, architecte; gravé par Hibon; Paris, chez B. Bance éditeur, rue Croix-des-Petits-Champs 23
images.shows: Wide Champs-Élysées frontage, arcaded ground floor, five storeys.
images.why_it_matters: Carries a printed SCALE BAR, so it is measurable. Calliat's own publication — a third publisher independent of both Daly and the Moniteur.

images.title: Élévation de la maison à l'angle de la rue Vivienne et du boulevard — plan sur le boulevard
images.publication: a drawn survey sheet, not an engraving; carries a red collection stamp
images.shows: A CORNER building drawn along its whole boulevard elevation — the pan coupé condition, at length.
images.why_it_matters: The register's corner evidence is otherwise one 340px thumbnail. This shows a corner's full run.
images.limits: Faint, and no scale bar located.

images.title: Measured elevation with dimension lines (unidentified)
images.publication: a measured survey drawing, not a published plate
images.shows: An elevation with DIMENSION LINES and callouts drawn on it, and shopfront details dimensioned below.
images.why_it_matters: Potentially the most useful of the batch if the callouts can be read at higher resolution — dimensioned drawings are what the sill question needs. Unidentified as it stands.
images.open_question: Can the dimension callouts be read? Not legible at this resolution.

crawl.why_so_few: 203 of 223 are not Paris apartment-building elevations at all -- they are monuments, churches, palaces, exposition pavilions, fountains, tombs and interiors. Of the 20 that matched, most are interiors, floor plans, photographs or hotels particuliers rather than immeubles.
crawl.rate_limited: ~1 s between page fetches, ~0.6 s between image fetches
